fullPassage:
My Octopus Teacher

I returned to the Cape of Good Hope, South Africa, where I had spent my childhood, after over 20 years of movie-making. I went diving in the cold sea off the coast of the Cape, and it was among the dense seaweed forests where I met an octopus.

First Encounter

I saw a fish peacefully swimming near a heap of shells. Suddenly, an octopus sprang from the heap and grabbed the fish. Amazed at the cleverness of the octopus, I swam a little closer, but it disappeared. In fact, it had lifted a piece of seaweed, wrapped it around itself, and was staring at me out of a little gap. What an extraordinary creature! I wondered what would happen if I kept watching it. To see the world from the octopus's perspective, I left a camera near the den and started visiting regularly. I even mapped the environment around the den. Expecting some drama to come, I waited.

Making Friends

The octopus became less scared as I visited more often. After about a month, it came near me. I put my hand out, and it reached out to me. After another week, it started to wave like a human friend saying, "Hi, I'm excited to see you." I kept still, and it covered my whole hand. Since I had to take a breath, I swam toward the surface. To my surprise, it rode on my hand all the way to the top. There I was, just staring into the eyes of this incredible creature. It sparked my curiosity in a way that I had not experienced before. Had I gained its trust? I started reading books about octopuses, but I wanted to learn more about this marvelous creature. The first thing I learned was that "it" was a "she."

Getting Closer

Danger in the form of pyjama sharks, the area's biggest predators, came with little warning in the sea. The octopus was moving around near the edge of the seaweed forest, and I saw a shark tracking her. In an instant, she swam into a crack to escape, but the shark was faster.

The shark had taken a bite of one of her arms and was waiting for her. I wanted to save my friend, but in this environment, I could only observe. She managed to get deeper into the crack, but she was bleeding. After a while, the shark lost interest, and the octopus used the opportunity to get back to her den, without one of her arms. She was in serious danger because her arms function like the hands, legs, nose, and eyes of humans.

The next day, I was relieved to see that she had survived. She was weak, and her colors were not as bright. I checked on her every day, wondering if that day would be the last. It was emotionally painful to witness these things happening to her.

Recovery, Growth, and Sacrifice

A short while later, I saw that the wound had healed. To my amazement, a little arm started to grow back, and she started to become active again. I started to compare my life to life in the unforgiving sea. I thought of what was valuable in life. I began to spend more time with my family and friends, and I even started to dive with my young son. He became just as interested in her as I was. As the octopus's arm became more functional, I felt things in my life were improving too.

An octopus's average life is about a year, which ends after reproducing. One day, eight months after meeting her, I found her with another octopus. It was bittersweet knowing her final days were approaching even though she would bear young.

After mating, she didn't come out of her den. There would be no feeding or hunting. She was timing her final moments for the hatching of her eggs. After the eggs hatched, she died. A few months later, my son found a little octopus. We believe her story continues on.

I fell in love with an octopus and the amazing wildness she represented. I built a relationship with her and witnessed her life up to the final moments. I saw her from a perspective that I could not have had without this experience. She was smart, sensitive, and strong, often going through rough and tough days just like humans do. Eventually, she committed herself to protecting the birth of her young before she died. As a human being, I found something noble in that sacrifice. She was not simply an octopus; she was a part of this world just as I am a part of it now, and in that sense, we all have our own stories to tell.

questions.passage: My Octopus Teacher I returned to the Cape of Good Hope, South Africa, where I had spent my childhood, after over 20 years of movie-making. I went diving in the cold sea off the coast of the Cape, and it was among the (A)[dense / sparse] seaweed forests where I met an octopus. I saw a fish peacefully swimming near a (B)[heap / lack] of shells. Suddenly, an octopus (C)[sprang / retreated] from the heap and grabbed the fish. Amazed at the cleverness of the octopus, I swam a little closer, but it disappeared. In fact, it had lifted a piece of seaweed, wrapped it around itself, and was staring at me out of a little gap.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 빽빽한(dense) 해조류 숲에서 문어를 만났고, 조개 더미(heap) 근처에서 문어가 튀어나왔다(sprang).
det.analysis:
✅ ① dense — heap — sprang: 원문 그대로의 표현
❌ ② sparse(드문): dense(빽빽한)의 반의어
❌ ③ lack(부족): heap(더미)과 반대 의미
❌ ④ retreated(후퇴했다): sprang(튀어나왔다)의 반의어
det.tip: dense(빽빽한) ↔ sparse(드문), heap(더미) ↔ lack(부족), spring-sprang(튀어나오다) ↔ retreat(후퇴하다)

questions.passage: What an extraordinary creature! I wondered what would happen if I kept watching it. To see the world from the octopus's (A)[perspective / prejudice], I left a camera near the den and started visiting (B)[regularly / rarely]. I even (C)[mapped / neglected] the environment around the den. Expecting some drama to come, I waited. Making Friends The octopus became less scared as I visited more often.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 문어의 관점(perspective)에서 세상을 보기 위해 카메라를 두고 정기적으로(regularly) 방문하기 시작했다. 굴 주변 환경을 지도로 만들었다(mapped).
det.analysis:
✅ ② perspective — regularly — mapped: 원문 그대로
❌ ① prejudice(편견): perspective(관점)와 혼동 유발이나 문맥상 부적절
❌ ③ rarely(드물게): regularly(정기적으로)의 반의어
❌ ④ neglected(방치했다): mapped(지도로 만들었다)의 반의어 맥락
det.tip: perspective(관점) vs prejudice(편견): 둘 다 per-/pre- 접두사. regularly ↔ rarely, map(동사: 지도화하다) ↔ neglect(방치하다)

questions.passage: I built a relationship with her and witnessed her life up to the final moments. I saw her from a perspective that I could not have had without this experience. She was smart, sensitive, and strong, often going through (A)[rough / smooth] and tough days just like humans do. Eventually, she (B)[committed / surrendered] herself to protecting the birth of her young before she died. As a human being, I found something (C)[noble / trivial] in that sacrifice. She was not simply an octopus; she was a part of this world just as I am a part of it now, and in that sense, we all have our own stories to tell.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 그녀는 인간처럼 거친(rough) 날들을 보냈다. 결국 새끼를 보호하는 데 헌신했다(committed). 나는 그 희생에서 고귀한(noble) 것을 발견했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ rough — committed — noble: 원문 그대로
❌ ① smooth(순탄한): rough(거친)의 반의어. 뒤의 tough와 병렬이므로 smooth는 부적절
❌ ② surrendered(항복했다): committed(헌신했다)의 반의어 맥락. trivial(하찮은): noble의 반의어
❌ ④ smooth + surrendered: 이중 오류
det.tip: rough and tough: 유사 의미 병렬 강조. commit oneself to ~ing: ~에 헌신하다. noble(고귀한) ↔ trivial(하찮은)

questions.passage: The octopus became less ①<u>scared</u> as I visited more often. After about a month, it came near me. I put my hand out, and it reached out to me. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 가장 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 문어는 방문할수록 덜 무서워했다. 호기심을 불러일으켰다. 내가 문어의 신뢰(trust)를 얻었을까? → distrust(불신)는 문맥상 부적절
det.analysis:
✅ ③ distrust(불신) → trust(신뢰): 화자가 문어와 친해진 맥락에서 '불신을 얻었나?'는 반대
❌ ① scared(무서워하는): 원문 그대로
❌ ② curiosity(호기심): 원문 그대로
❌ ④ marvelous(놀라운): 원문 그대로
det.tip: trust(신뢰) ↔ distrust(불신). gain one's trust: ~의 신뢰를 얻다

questions.passage: Danger in the form of pyjama sharks, the area's biggest ①<u>predators</u>, came with little warning in the sea. The octopus was moving around near the edge of the seaweed forest. After a while, the shark lost ④<u>appetite</u>, and the octopus used the opportunity to get back to her den.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 가장 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 파자마 상어는 그 지역 최대 포식자였다. 문어는 틈으로 헤엄쳐 탈출했지만 상어가 더 빨랐다. 그녀는 더 깊이 들어가는 데 성공했다. 상어가 흥미(interest)를 잃었다 → appetite(식욕)는 부적절
det.analysis:
✅ ④ appetite(식욕) → interest(흥미): 원문은 'the shark lost interest'. appetite는 '식욕'으로 문맥상 어색
❌ ① predators(포식자): 원문 그대로
❌ ② escape(탈출하다): 원문 그대로
❌ ③ managed(성공했다): 원문 그대로
det.tip: lose interest(흥미를 잃다) vs lose appetite(식욕을 잃다). predator(포식자) ↔ prey(먹이)

questions.passage: I started to compare my life to life in the ①<u>unforgiving</u> sea. I thought of what was ②<u>valuable</u> in life. I began to spend more time with my family and friends. As the octopus's arm became more ③<u>functional</u>, I felt things in my life were ④<u>deteriorating</u> too.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 가장 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 냉혹한 바다에서의 삶과 비교하기 시작했다. 삶에서 소중한 것을 생각했다. 문어의 팔이 더 기능적이 되면서 내 삶도 나아지고(improving) 있다고 느꼈다 → deteriorating(악화)는 반대
det.analysis:
✅ ④ deteriorating(악화되는) → improving(나아지는): 문어 회복과 화자의 삶이 동시에 나아지는 맥락
❌ ① unforgiving(냉혹한): 원문 그대로
❌ ② valuable(소중한): 원문 그대로
❌ ③ functional(기능적인): 원문 그대로
det.tip: improve(나아지다) ↔ deteriorate(악화되다). unforgiving: '용서 없는' → 비유적으로 '냉혹한'

questions.passage:
My Octopus Teacher

I returned to the Cape of Good Hope, South Africa, where I had spent my childhood, after over 20 years of movie-making. I went diving in the cold sea off the coast of the Cape, and it was among the dense seaweed forests where I met an octopus.

First Encounter

I saw a fish peacefully swimming near a heap of shells. Suddenly, an octopus sprang from the heap and <u>grabbed</u> the fish. Amazed at the cleverness of the octopus, I swam a little closer, but it disappeared. In fact, it had lifted a piece of seaweed, wrapped it around itself, and was staring at me out of a little gap. What an extraordinary creature! I wondered what would happen if I kept watching it. To see the world from the octopus's perspective, I left a camera near the den and started visiting regularly. I even mapped the environment around the den. Expecting some drama to come, I waited.

Making Friends

The octopus became less scared as I visited more often. After about a month, it came near me. I put my hand out, and it reached out to me. After another week, it started to wave like a human friend saying, "Hi, I'm excited to see you." I kept still, and it covered my whole hand. Since I had to take a breath, I swam toward the surface. To my surprise, it rode on my hand all the way to the top. There I was, just staring into the eyes of this incredible creature. It sparked my curiosity in a way that I had not experienced before. Had I gained its trust? I started reading books about octopuses, but I wanted to learn more about this marvelous creature. The first thing I learned was that "it" was a "she."

Getting Closer

Danger in the form of pyjama sharks, the area's biggest predators, came with little warning in the sea. The octopus was moving around near the edge of the seaweed forest, and I saw a shark tracking her. In an instant, she swam into a crack to escape, but the shark was faster.

The shark had taken a bite of one of her arms and was waiting for her. I wanted to save my friend, but in this environment, I could only observe. She managed to get deeper into the crack, but she was bleeding. After a while, the shark lost interest, and the octopus used the opportunity to get back to her den, without one of her arms. She was in serious danger because her arms function like the hands, legs, nose, and eyes of humans.

The next day, I was relieved to see that she had survived. She was weak, and her colors were not as bright. I checked on her every day, wondering if that day would be the last. It was emotionally painful to witness these things happening to her.

Recovery, Growth, and Sacrifice

A short while later, I saw that the wound had healed. To my amazement, a little arm started to grow back, and she started to become active again. I started to compare my life to life in the unforgiving sea. I thought of what was valuable in life. I began to spend more time with my family and friends, and I even started to dive with my young son. He became just as interested in her as I was. As the octopus's arm became more functional, I felt things in my life were improving too.

An octopus's average life is about a year, which ends after reproducing. One day, eight months after meeting her, I found her with another octopus. It was bittersweet knowing her final days were approaching even though she would bear young.

After mating, she didn't come out of her den. There would be no feeding or hunting. She was timing her final moments for the hatching of her eggs. After the eggs hatched, she died. A few months later, my son found a little octopus. We believe her story continues on.

I fell in love with an octopus and the amazing wildness she represented. I built a relationship with her and witnessed her life up to the final moments. I saw her from a perspective that I could not have had without this experience. She was smart, sensitive, and strong, often going through rough and tough days just like humans do. Eventually, she committed herself to protecting the birth of her young before she died. As a human being, I found something noble in that sacrifice. She was not simply an octopus; she was a part of this world just as I am a part of it now, and in that sense, we all have our own stories to tell.

❌ ③ avoided(피하다): 의미 반대
❌ ④ dropped(떨어뜨리다): grabbed의 반의어 맥락

questions.stem: 다음 두 문장에서 밑줄 친 (A) function과 (B) functional의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) 그녀의 팔은 인간의 손, 다리, 코, 눈처럼 기능한다. (B) 문어의 팔이 더 기능을 하는 상태가 되면서
det.analysis:
✅ ③ (A) 기능하다 — (B) 기능을 하는: (A)는 동사 function(기능하다), (B)는 형용사 functional(기능을 수행하는)
❌ ① 행사(function의 다른 뜻): 문맥상 동사로 쓰임
❌ ② (B) 실용적인: functional의 다른 뜻이지만 여기서는 '회복되어 기능하는'
❌ ④ (A) 행사: 동사 쓰임에 맞지 않음
det.tip: function: (명) 기능/행사/함수, (동) 기능하다. functional: (형) 기능적인/실용적인. 문맥에 따라 다의어 해석이 달라짐

✅ ④ perspective(관점): 영영 풀이와 정확히 일치
❌ ① perception(인식): 감각적 인식이지 관점이 아님
❌ ③ perfection(완벽): 의미 다름
❌ ② permission(허가): 의미 다름

det.korean: 문어의 영리함(cleverness)에 놀라 더 가까이 헤엄쳤다.
det.analysis: ✅ cleverness: 전치사 at 뒤 + the + ____이므로 명사 필요. clever(형용사) → cleverness(명사)
det.tip: 형용사 → 명사: clever → cleverness, happy → happiness, kind → kindness (-ness 접미사)

questions.passage: I built a relationship with her and witnessed her life up to the final moments. I fell in love with an octopus and the amazing __________ (wild) she represented.
questions.stem: 다음 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (1단어) (영어로) (   ) 쓰시오.

det.korean: 알이 부화한 후 죽었다. 나는 문어와 그녀가 대표하는 놀라운 야생성(wildness)에 빠졌다.
det.analysis: ✅ wildness: the amazing ____ 구조에서 관사+형용사 뒤 명사 필요. wild(형용사) → wildness(명사)
det.tip: wild(야생의/거친) → wildness(야생/거침). 'the + 형용사 + 명사' 패턴

questions.passage:
My Octopus Teacher

I returned to the Cape of Good Hope, South Africa, where I had spent my childhood, after over 20 years of movie-making. I went diving in the cold sea off the coast of the Cape, and it was among the dense seaweed forests where I met an octopus.

First Encounter

I saw a fish peacefully swimming near a heap of shells. Suddenly, an octopus sprang from the heap and grabbed the fish. Amazed at the cleverness of the octopus, I swam a little closer, but it disappeared. In fact, it had lifted a piece of seaweed, wrapped it around itself, and was staring at me out of a little gap. What an extraordinary creature! I wondered what would happen if I kept watching it. To see the world from the octopus's perspective, I left a camera near the den and started visiting regularly. I even mapped the environment around the den. Expecting some drama to come, I waited.

Making Friends

The octopus became less scared as I visited more often. After about a month, it came near me. I put my hand out, and it reached out to me. After another week, it started to wave like a human friend saying, "Hi, I'm excited to see you." I kept still, and it covered my whole hand. Since I had to take a breath, I swam toward the surface. To my surprise, it rode on my hand all the way to the top. There I was, just staring into the eyes of this incredible creature. It sparked my curiosity in a way that I had not experienced before. Had I gained its trust? I started reading books about octopuses, but I wanted to learn more about this marvelous creature. The first thing I learned was that "it" was a "she."

Getting Closer

Danger in the form of pyjama sharks, the area's biggest predators, came with little warning in the sea. The octopus was moving around near the edge of the seaweed forest, and I saw a shark tracking her. In an instant, she swam into a crack to escape, but the shark was faster.

The shark had taken a bite of one of her arms and was waiting for her. I wanted to save my friend, but in this environment, I could only observe. She managed to get deeper into the crack, but she was bleeding. After a while, the shark lost interest, and the octopus used the opportunity to get back to her den, without one of her arms. She was in serious danger because her arms function like the hands, legs, nose, and eyes of humans.

The next day, I was relieved to see that she had survived. She was weak, and her colors were not as bright. I checked on her every day, wondering if that day would be the last. It was emotionally painful to witness these things happening to her.

Recovery, Growth, and Sacrifice

A short while later, I saw that the wound had healed. To my amazement, a little arm started to grow back, and she started to become active again. I started to compare my life to life in the unforgiving sea. I thought of what was valuable in life. I began to spend more time with my family and friends, and I even started to dive with my young son. He became just as interested in her as I was. As the octopus's arm became more functional, I felt things in my life were improving too.

An octopus's average life is about a year, which ends after reproducing. One day, eight months after meeting her, I found her with another octopus. It was bittersweet knowing her final days were approaching even though she would bear young.

After mating, she didn't come out of her den. There would be no feeding or hunting. She was timing her final moments for ____. After the eggs hatched, she died. A few months later, my son found a little octopus. We believe her story continues on.

I fell in love with an octopus and the amazing wildness she represented. I built a relationship with her and witnessed her life up to the final moments. I saw her from a perspective that I could not have had without this experience. She was smart, sensitive, and strong, often going through rough and tough days just like humans do. Eventually, she committed herself to protecting the birth of her young before she died. As a human being, I found something noble in that sacrifice. She was not simply an octopus; she was a part of this world just as I am a part of it now, and in that sense, we all have our own stories to tell.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 짝짓기 후, 굴에서 나오지 않았다. 먹이 활동도 사냥도 없었다. 마지막 순간을 알의 부화(the hatching of her eggs)에 맞추고 있었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① the hatching of her eggs: 원문 그대로의 표현
❌ ③ the arrival of the shark: 이 시점의 맥락과 무관
❌ ② the changing of the season: 본문에 언급 없음
❌ ④ the growth of her arms: 이전 단락 내용
det.tip: hatch: (알이) 부화하다. timing ~ for: ~에 맞추어 시간을 조절하다. mate: 짝짓기하다

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: a dangerous creature in the sea
a part of this world just as I am a part of it now
an animal I studied for research
a teacher who gave me lessons

det.korean: 그녀의 삶을 마지막 순간까지 목격했다. 이 경험 없이는 가질 수 없었을 관점으로 보았다. 그녀는 단순히 문어가 아니었다; 내가 지금 이 세상의 일부인 것처럼 이 세상의 일부였다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② a part of this world just as I am a part of it now: 원문 그대로
❌ ① a dangerous creature: 화자의 감정과 반대
❌ ④ an animal I studied for research: 연구가 아닌 관계 형성
❌ ③ a teacher who gave me lessons: 비유적이나 원문의 정확한 표현이 아님
det.tip: not simply A; she was B: A가 아니라 B라는 대조 구문. just as ~: ~처럼
